In the heart of Hanoi, the capital of Vietnam, lies the iconic Walking Street, also known as Phố đi bộ, a pedestrian haven that pulsates with cultural vibrancy every weekend. This enchanting space, encircling the serene Hoan Kiem Lake, has been transformed into a pedestrian street since 2016, reviving the sacred essence of the legend of King Le Loi returning the precious sword to the golden turtle of yesteryear.

Walking Street, also known as the pedestrian area around Hoan Kiem Lake in Hanoi, is a vibrant and bustling destination that immerses visitors into the heart of Vietnam's rich history and culture. This iconic pedestrian zone, which includes several streets such as Pho Ding Tien Hoang, Pho Hang Kay, Pho Le Thai To, Pho Le Lai, Pho Le Thach, Pho Tran Nguyen Han, Pho Ding Le, Pho Nguyen Xi, Pho Trang Tien, Pho Lo Su, Pho Hang Dau, Pho Hoan Kiem, Pho Luong Van Can, Pho Hang Bai, and Pho Bao Khanh, transforms into a lively hub every Friday evening from 7 PM until midnight on Sunday.

The concept of a walking street was first tested in Hà Nội in 2004 along Hàng Đào and Đồng Xuân streets, and later expanded to the first-level preservation area in 2014, which included Hàng Buồm, Hàng Giầy, Lương Ngọc Quyến, Mã Mây, Đào Duy Từ, and Tạ Hiện streets. The current Walking Street around Hoàn Kiếm Lake officially began operations on September 1, 2016.
